Jeremy Scahill is absolutely right, and articulating a truth that many Palestine advocates like Cenk Uyghur and Mehdi Hasan shy away from.

The point is not that Palestinians should use violence, much less that they should commit war-crimes (Scahill is careful to talk only about attacking soldiers).

The point is that the Occupation can be legally resisted by using violence. Palestinians have a right to fight back the same as any other occupied people.

Once you fail to articulate that right, you cede the ground to Zionists to claim that Palestinian use of violence is ipso facto terrorism, and thereby to claim that violence is unrelated to a legitimate resistance, but an expression of - say - anti-Semitism, or religious fanaticism, or barbarism, or some such other species of b.s.. 

Failing to articulate a right to violent resistance removes the focus from where it belongs - the unjustified violence of the Occupation - by allowing Palestinian violent resistance to be characterised as unjustified, and therefore the violence of the Occupier to be presented as justified.
